name: Zeror
overview: Zeror was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, recognized primarily as the father of Abiel and an ancestor of King Saul. His role is noted in the genealogical context of the early monarchy of Israel. Scripture does not provide additional personal details or narratives about his life.
namesAndTitles: The name Zeror means 'money bag,' 'pouch,' or possibly 'pebbles' in Hebrew, reflecting a common practice of meaningful naming in the Old Testament. This proper name is not indicated to have been given directly by God but carries connotations that may relate to provision or value.
familyAndRelationships: Zeror is explicitly identified as the father of Becorath and is inferred to be the father of Abiel, situating him within the lineage leading to King Saul. These relationships emphasize his place in the ancestral line of significant biblical figures from the tribe of Benjamin.
scriptureSignificance: Zeror holds importance in the biblical narrative as a patriarchal figure within the tribe of Benjamin, connecting the genealogy that leads to Israel's first king, Saul. His mention in 1 Samuel 9:1 places him within the historical framework that establishes Saul's royal heritage. Though not a central character in biblical events, his genealogical role supports the providential unfolding of God's plan for Israel's monarchy.
